body: T17 - CORRECT ANSWER ANIMATION FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES. COGNITIVE NEED: Kai answered correctly. His brain needs confirmation within 500ms or the reward signal degrades (Volkow 2011). The signal must be: visually unambiguous, emotionally positive, not distracting from the next question. MECHANISM: Green flash on the answered card. Green = right (universal and culturally consistent). Flash = instant event not a lingering state. Not distracting because it is contained to the card boundary, not full-screen. VALUE: The animation delivers three things simultaneously: confirmation (you got it), location (this card is done), and permission to move (the card is settled, move on). Without animation the card just changes color and Kai must cognitively re-evaluate whether the state changed. The animation signals state change without requiring evaluation. DERIVATION: Why 800ms not 500ms. 500ms would feel too fast to register. 800ms is within the elevated engagement window (Barkley: 2-3 seconds after correct). It completes before attention drifts. Why pulse not fade. Fade is ambiguous (is it wrong or just fading?). Pulse is an event: started, peaked, done. Event signals are clearer than gradual changes for ADHD attention. Why green not Pistons red. Red is wrong. Green is right. We do not use brand color to signal correct - we use semantic color. The brand serves the experience not the other way around.
